verdict: The four scripts do what their specs say on every tested behaviour: 91 tests pass, 0 fail, 8 are skipped because they need the app. 26 mutations were tried and 21 were caught. The 5 survivors are test gaps: the record sha re-check in compare (CM3), the blind order's dependence on the plan hash (CM7), the audit's epoch binding in gate (GT7), the sample sd (KC2) and the context-fall filter for g (KC3) in cost. There are no high findings. There are 14 medium ones. Two are code defects in compare: an unbound attempt gives tokens 0 instead of transcript-missing, and the scorer's result is not checked for completeness. Compare also has a race (the plan binding is not re-checked under the lock) and a liveness fault (an anon run on some of the arms locks the key). Four are design or spec gaps: an owner approval is not bound to the draft's content, a hazard can be rewritten under its old id, G1-G12 are never required, and the blind order can be computed from public values. Three are test gaps for the surviving mutations. Two are fail-open reads in cost: card objects read without a hash check, and default inputs probed outside tcb/. One brief tells the S1 session that it is the control. Nothing was written outside review-tmp/U5 and done/review-U5.json. The return is at C:/Users/User/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/192654871f6b1294/e24f17dc-4aea-4914-a9d1-280a723d620e/scratchpad/tcb-build/done/review-U5.json.

tests.command: node tools/lane.mjs --label review-U5 --timeout-s 300 -- node --test --test-concurrency=1 tcb/test/<protocol-freeze|compare|gate|cost>.test.mjs (one file per lane call)
tests.output_tail: protocol-freeze: tests 28, pass 26, skipped 2; compare: tests 24, pass 22, skipped 2; gate: tests 24, pass 22, skipped 2; cost: tests 23, pass 21, skipped 2. Every skip is an NA test that needs the app.

mutations.what: PF2 owner line need not follow last freeze/amend (seq check dropped)
CM1 arm names not scrubbed from blinded text
CM7 blind seed independent of plan hash (line 669)
GT1 any accept line covers every high hazard
GT5 outputs not bound to current cut sha
GT7 audit not bound to committed epoch (line 283)
KC1 missing transcripts no longer untrusted
KC2 sample sd divides by n (line 572)
KC3 context falls averaged into g (line 746)
KC4 predict n_cap off by one
KC6 meter window includes first-line calls

findings.claim: An attempt with no session whose folder has no transcript, and a task with no row, add 0 tokens and are not marked missing. Tokens, confirmed_per_extra_million_tokens and prediction.actual come out too low, and the check line says pass.
findings.evidence: Only the a.session branch sets missing (line 303). In the a.folder branch an empty or failing transcriptsForFolder (lines 309-313) leaves missing false. rows.get(task) undefined is not flagged. The spec requires tokens null and reason transcript-missing:<task>.
findings.fix: Set missing = true when a row is absent, or when an attempt has neither a session main transcript nor a folder transcript. Fall back to the folder when the session's main transcript is absent.

findings.claim: The ledger, plan binding, certificates and commits are read before run.lock. comparison.json and the check line are written under the lock without checking that the ledger has not moved, so an analysis-plan amend that lands in between gives a 'descriptive' label bound to a superseded plan sha.
findings.evidence: loadLedger and bindPlan run at lines 732-733 with no lock. Under the lock, the ledger is re-read only to find the previous check line (line 779).
findings.fix: Keep the snapshot's ledger head (seq and hash). Under the lock, if the head changed, return exit 75 (or recompute once) and write nothing, in both anon and score.

findings.claim: The scorer's result is not checked for completeness. A result with items left out, or with guess_arm outside the arm names, is still 'scored'. rate is computed over the items returned, so one confident item gives rate 1.
findings.evidence: Line 444 rejects only unknown or duplicate items. seen.size is never compared with the key's items, and guess_arm is never checked. The scorer brief demands exactly one entry per item.
findings.fix: Return scores-invalid (not_run) unless seen.size equals the number of key items and every guess_arm is one of the key's arms. Add both cases to T13.

findings.claim: The blind order can be computed from values that are not sealed. The seed is sha256('blind:'+plan_sha256): the plan sha is in the ledger and plan/frozen/, the arm names are in views/blind/index.json, and lib.rng is public. The coordinator profile reads plan/ and views/ and has Bash, so the sealed key adds no secrecy. Mutation CM7, which made the seed independent of the plan hash, also survived.
findings.evidence: Line 669. coordinator.json read_prefixes include {root}/plan/ and {root}/views/, with bash tcb-node. With CM7, all tests passed.
findings.fix: On the first anon, draw the seed with crypto.randomBytes and store it only in the sealed key. On a repeat, reuse the seed from the existing key so the bytes stay identical. Amend the spec. In T3, assert that the order differs between two plan hashes.

findings.claim: If anon runs while only some arms are committed, it creates the exclusive key for that plan. Every later full anon exits 1 blind-key-differs, and exit 1 is not among compare's exit codes. The remaining arms can then never be blinded under that plan.
findings.evidence: live holds only the committed arms (line 665). The key is created exclusively and never replaced (lines 758-761). Line 751 throws exit 1.
findings.fix: Refuse anon with exit 2 (arms-not-committed) unless every arm in arm_tasks has a committed review.

findings.claim: Mutation CM3 survived: no test catches a commit record whose outputs[].id points to another valid object while keeping the old sha256.
findings.evidence: T16 edits only object bytes, which getObject's name check already catches. With line 125 disabled, all tests passed.
findings.fix: Add a T16 case: the record's review id is swapped for a second valid review object. Expect exit 3 object-mismatch.

findings.claim: Approval is bound to subject and quote text only, not to the draft's content. A draft edited after the owner approved it, with the same approval.quote, freezes as owner-approved.
findings.evidence: The owner line is {act, subject, quote} with no hash. The match (lines 357-359) compares act, subject, clip500(quote) and seq. For a first freeze, after = 0, so any earlier approve line with that quote serves.
findings.fix: Have status.mjs record the sha256 of the canonical draft in the approve line, and have protocol-freeze require it to equal the sha256 of the draft it freezes (approval-unrecorded otherwise). This is a contract change.

findings.claim: Design R55 requires every high hazard, gaps G1-G12 included, to be covered or accepted. The gate requires only P1..P21 in p_ids, so a mapper that leaves G1-G12 out still passes.
findings.evidence: Line 341 loops over P1..P21 only. Design lines 517-518 and 599-612 define G1-G12 as problem-table rows.
findings.fix: Also require G1..G12 in p_ids (p-id-missing), or read the required ids from the problems table that is handed to the mapper. Fix the spec line.

findings.claim: The append-only check tests only that parent ids are present. A child can keep h3 and rewrite its statement or severity, and an earlier owner accept for hazard:h3 then covers text the owner never saw.
findings.evidence: dropped (line 331) collects only parent ids absent from the child. accepted (lines 347-349) takes any owner accept subject, regardless of when it was written.
findings.fix: Require each parent hazard's classical_name, statement and severity to be unchanged under the same id in the child (only status, covered_by and p_ids may change); otherwise add hazards-not-append-only. Alternatively, bind the accept to the hazard's canonical sha.

findings.claim: Mutation GT7 survived: the audit line's epoch binding is untested. A clean audit of another epoch would clear analysis-tainted for the committed epoch, and no test would notice.
findings.evidence: With the epoch match removed, T5 and T12 passed.
findings.fix: Add T12 cases: stpa committed at epoch 2 with a clean audit for epoch 1 only gives exit 2 audit-missing; a tainted epoch-2 line followed by a clean epoch-1 line gives exit 1.

findings.claim: Card objects are read with lib.readJson straight from store/objects, without getObject's name check and without comparing against the commit record's sha256. Unreadable records and cards are dropped silently, so a changed card shifts t_q and k_q (read by admission, R47) and no reason says why.
findings.evidence: Line 717 reads with lib.readJson, and the catches at lines 699-701 and 719-721 swallow every error. The spec reads card objects through the commit records.
findings.fix: Use lib.getObject and compare against output.sha256. On any failure, add the task and id to an 'unreadable' list and set trusted false (exit 2).

findings.claim: Two survivors. KC2 (sd divided by n) survived because no unit with n >= 2 is asserted. KC3 (falls averaged into g) survived because T10's median over [2800, 3000, 3200] hides epoch 1's mean of -4880, although the assertion claims the fall is not averaged.
findings.evidence: Only sd === null is asserted. The median of [-4880, 3000, 3200] is still 3000.
findings.fix: Assert sd on a two-task unit (100 and 300 give 141.42). Assert g on a role with a single session that contains the fall.

findings.claim: compute first probes <script dir>/../cost-inputs.json. In the flat layout that is the run root, outside tcb/ and with no single writer, and a file there silently replaces the owner-approved tcb/cost-inputs.json.
findings.evidence: Line 1041 is checked with existsSync before HERE/cost-inputs.json.

findings.claim: The child brief tells the S1 arm that it is the 'control' (line 42 says 'Role `control`: you start no readers...', and line 3 renders {{role}} = control). That reveals the comparison to an arm under test, against spec/briefs.md's rule that no brief mentions that anything is tested.
findings.evidence: child.md line 42. CONTRACT line 298 lists role 'control', and the brief prints {{role}}.
findings.fix: Show a neutral label (for example 'solo') in place of the role name, and phrase line 42 as 'If your manifest lists no reader agent type, you start no readers'.
